cards.text: Nehemiah, the king's cupbearer (Nehemiah 1:11), got word that Jerusalem's wall is broken down and its gates burned (Nehemiah 1:3). Now it's the month of Nisan, and he hands wine to Artaxerxes, king of Persia (Ezra 7:1). He has never once been sad in front of this king, until today.

cards.question: King Artaxerxes can tell Nehemiah isn't ill. So what does the king say must be behind that sad face?
When King Artaxerxes asks about his sad face, Nehemiah stays calm and cool.

cards.text: Nehemiah is overwhelmed with fear. Me? If a king looked at me like that, my mustache would already be packing my bags.
But he answers anyway. He starts with "May the king live forever!" and then tells the king exactly why he's sad.

cards.question: Nehemiah explains his sadness to King Artaxerxes. How does he describe Jerusalem?

answers.text: The city where his fathers are buried
The city where he was born
The city where he first served

cards.text: The king asks, "What is your request?" Friend, that's the boss leaning back in his chair going, "Okay, talk to me."

cards.question: King Artaxerxes just asked Nehemiah what he wants. What does Nehemiah do before he answers?

answers.text: Prays to the God of heaven
Asks the queen to speak for him
Asks for a night to think

cards.question: Nehemiah asks the king to send him to Judah, to the city where his fathers are buried, so he can ___ it.
With the queen seated beside him, King Artaxerxes asks how long Nehemiah's journey will take and when he'll return.

cards.text: It pleases the king to send him, and Nehemiah sets a time. Every boss in history: "Sure, go. Just tell me when you're BACK."

cards.question: Nehemiah isn't done asking. He wants letters for the governors west of the Euphrates. What are those letters for?

answers.text: So they'll grant him safe passage

cards.question: Nehemiah also wants a letter to Asaph, keeper of the king's forest, so Asaph will give him ___ to make beams for the gates of the citadel to the temple, the city wall and his house.
King Artaxerxes grants all of Nehemiah's requests. Why does Nehemiah say it happened?

answers.text: The gracious hand of his God was on him
He had served the king for years
The queen spoke up for him

cards.text: So Nehemiah goes to the governors west of the Euphrates and hands them the king's letters. This man walked in to pour a drink and walked OUT with travel papers and a lumber order.

cards.question: King Artaxerxes sends Nehemiah off on his trip without any soldiers.

cards.text: But not everybody's celebrating. Two new names show up, Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite official, and they hear about all of this.

cards.question: Sanballat and Tobiah are deeply ___ that someone has come to seek the ___ of the Israelites.

cards.text: Nehemiah's on his way, and two men are already upset about it. Pull up a chair, friend, because this story's just getting warmed up.

findings.problem: Card 3 already asked whether Nehemiah stays calm, and its answer (False) shows he isn't. Card 4 then opens by restating that same fact from Nehemiah 2:2, 'Nehemiah is overwhelmed with fear,' and adds a joke. Nothing new in the passage happens on this card, so it doesn't move the baker forward. The joke could ride on card 5 instead, or the T/F could be turned into a story beat.

rule.text:
Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.
- No recap cards.

findings.problem: The card asks how Nehemiah describes Jerusalem, with the answer 'The city where his fathers are buried.' No earlier card mentions his fathers or their graves, so the baker can only guess Nehemiah's exact phrase, not reason it out. The heart of verse 3 is why he's sad: the city lies in ruins and its gates are burned. That would make a better question if it is set up without the answer being given away.

rule.text:
These rules apply to every passage, of any type:
- **Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.**

findings.problem: The question itself says Asaph is 'keeper of the king's forest' and that the material is 'to make beams.' Those words rule out 'stone' and 'bronze,' so the right answer is given away in the setup.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The first sentence, 'Nehemiah's on his way, and two men are already upset about it,' just restates what card 18 answered (Nehemiah 2:10) before the story-continues line. Since verse 10 is already asked on card 18, this card can be just the story-continues line.
